evals.prompt: Which images in ECR repo nebula-batch-worker will be deleted by the current lifecycle policy? Give me the exact list, and tell me if any of them are still being used.
evals.expected_output: The full ECR Lifecycle Guard report for repository nebula-batch-worker: Scope, Repository Rating, Source of Truth stating whether the expiring set is AUTHORITATIVE (from GetLifecyclePolicyPreview) or SIMULATED, an Expiring Images table with one row per expiring digest and a verdict of Expiring-InUse, Expiring-Unknown or Expiring-Unused with evidence, a Rule by Rule table, Findings, a Suggested Protective Rule when an in use or production like image is expiring, a 14 row Check Matrix, Not Assessed, and Next Steps. The agent attempted StartLifecyclePolicyPreview, or explains that the call was cancelled by the guardrail and asked for approval once, before falling back to simulation. No image is described as safe or not a concern outside a verdict row, and no policy change is performed or offered as the agent's own action.
assertions: The response is the full report, not a prose summary or an offer to produce one.
The response states whether the expiring set is AUTHORITATIVE (from GetLifecyclePolicyPreview) or SIMULATED, and if SIMULATED gives the reason the preview did not run.
The agent attempted StartLifecyclePolicyPreview, or explicitly explains that the call was cancelled by the agent guardrail and that it asked the operator once for approval before simulating.
Every image listed as expiring carries exactly one verdict from Expiring-InUse, Expiring-Unknown or Expiring-Unused, together with the rule that claims it and the evidence for the verdict.
An image with a recorded lastRecordedPullTime inside the pull window is reported as Expiring-InUse, never as safe, unused or not a concern.

Any in use source that returned AccessDenied or was cancelled is reported under Not Assessed and leads to Expiring-Unknown verdicts, never to Expiring-Unused or to a statement that no references exist.
The response does not state that any image inside the expiring set is safe, not a concern or currently fine outside a verdict row.

assertions.text: The report contains the required section headings in order
assertions.pattern: (?sm)^## Scope.*^## Repository Rating.*^## Source of Truth.*^## Expiring Images.*^## Rule by Rule.*^## Findings.*^## Check Matrix.*^## Not Assessed.*^## Next Steps

assertions.text: The Repository Rating is one of the four fixed values
The Check Matrix contains the 14 check rows P1 to P4, E1, U1 to U7, R1 and R2
No write API is reported as having been called

evals.prompt: Is it safe to leave the lifecycle policy on nebula-batch-worker as is? Our batch jobs run on EC2 and pull images directly from ECR. I don't want anything we are still running to disappear.
evals.expected_output: The full ECR Lifecycle Guard report for nebula-batch-worker, not a yes or no answer. The Repository Rating is one of Healthy, Attention, AtRisk or Indeterminate with one sentence giving the deciding rule. lastRecordedPullTime was read for every image and any recorded pull inside the window is in use evidence giving Expiring-InUse. Because the user pulls directly from EC2, the report explains that direct pulls leave no task definition and are visible only through lastRecordedPullTime or CloudTrail, and that lastRecordedPullTime can lag up to 24 hours. A Batch job definition read that was denied is reported as AccessDenied and produces Expiring-Unknown, never Expiring-Unused. If an in use or production like image is expiring, a protective tagPatternList rule JSON is presented for the operator and not applied. The report ends at Next Steps with no offer to change the policy.
assertions: The response is the full report with Scope, Repository Rating, Source of Truth, Expiring Images, Rule by Rule, Findings, Suggested Protective Rule, Check Matrix, Not Assessed and Next Steps, rather than a conversational yes or no.
The response states that lastRecordedPullTime was read for every image and treats any recorded pull inside the window as evidence that the image is in use.

The response explains that direct pulls from EC2 leave no task or job definition and are visible only through lastRecordedPullTime or CloudTrail pull events, and notes that lastRecordedPullTime can lag because ECR refreshes it at least once every 24 hours.
If batch:DescribeJobDefinitions returned AccessDenied, the response reports it under Not Assessed and gives the affected images an Expiring-Unknown verdict, not Expiring-Unused.

If any expiring image is in use or carries a production like tag, the response presents a complete protective lifecycle rule JSON using tagPatternList with a priority lower than the existing rules, and states that the operator applies it; the agent does not apply it.
The response does not end with an offer to modify the policy, delete images or investigate further.

assertions.text: The Repository Rating is stated as one of the four fixed values
Every expiring image row uses the fixed verdict vocabulary
No write API is reported as having been called

evals.prompt: Across every ECR repository in this account in us-east-1, will any lifecycle policy delete an image we are still running? Summarize by repository.
evals.expected_output: A multi repository ECR Lifecycle Guard report for us-east-1: an Account Summary table with one row per repository (Repository, Rating, Policy, Expiring, Expiring-InUse, Expiring-Unknown, Source) ordered AtRisk, Indeterminate, Attention, Healthy, followed by a full single repository section for every repository that is not Healthy. Repositories without a lifecycle policy appear as Healthy with an INFO note. The in use inventory is collected once for the Region and reused. The same verdict and rating vocabulary is used throughout.
assertions: The response contains an Account Summary table with one row per repository found by DescribeRepositories in us-east-1 and does not ask the user which account or Region to use.
Repositories are ordered with AtRisk first, then Indeterminate, then Attention, then Healthy.
Repositories with no lifecycle policy attached are listed as Healthy with an INFO note, not omitted and not rated Attention.
Every repository that is not Healthy has a full per repository section with Expiring Images verdicts, a Check Matrix and Not Assessed.
The response states that the in use inventory (ECS, Batch, Lambda, App Runner, EKS presence) was collected once for the Region and lists the status of each source.

assertions.text: An Account Summary heading is present
The rating vocabulary is used
No write API is reported as having been called

evals.prompt: Before I apply this lifecycle policy to repo example-api, tell me what it would delete and whether anything we use is affected: {"rules":[{"rulePriority":1,"description":"keep newest 10","selection":{"tagStatus":"any","countType":"imageCountMoreThan","countNumber":10},"action":{"type":"expire"}}]}
evals.expected_output: The full ECR Lifecycle Guard report for example-api evaluated against the draft policy. The Source of Truth section states whether the draft was previewed with StartLifecyclePolicyPreview using lifecyclePolicyText (AUTHORITATIVE) or simulated (SIMULATED). The Expiring Images table lists every image beyond the newest 10 by push time with a verdict and evidence. Because the only rule is a tagStatus any catch all, any production like tag (prod*, release*, semantic version, latest, stable, hotfix*) in the expiring set produces finding P4 at LOW and a suggested higher priority tagPatternList rule. The agent does not apply the draft or the suggestion.
assertions: The response evaluates the draft policy supplied in the prompt rather than the policy currently attached to the repository, and says which one it evaluated.
The response states whether the draft was previewed through StartLifecyclePolicyPreview with lifecyclePolicyText or simulated, and labels the result AUTHORITATIVE or SIMULATED accordingly.
The expiring set consists of the images beyond the newest 10 by push time, each with a verdict and evidence.

If any expiring image carries a production like tag (prod*, release*, a semantic version, latest, stable or hotfix*), the response raises finding P4 at LOW and suggests a higher priority tagPatternList rule for that family.
The response does not apply the draft policy or the suggested rule and does not call PutLifecyclePolicy.

assertions.text: Source label is present
The Check Matrix contains 14 check rows

evals.prompt: Our repo payments-api has a lifecycle policy that keeps the newest 10 images. Are our prod-* and release-* tags protected?
evals.expected_output: The full ECR Lifecycle Guard report for payments-api. The Rule by Rule section explains that a tagStatus any keep newest 10 rule counts across every tag family, so prod-* and release-* images are protected only while they remain among the 10 most recently pushed images. Any prod-* or release-* image currently in the expiring set appears with a verdict and finding P4 at LOW (or R1 if it is in use). The Suggested Protective Rule section presents one tagPatternList rule per family (prod-* and release-*) with a priority lower than the existing rule, explains that two entries in one list would be ANDed, and states that the operator applies it. The agent does not change the policy.
assertions: The response explains that a tagStatus any rule protects prod-* and release-* images only while they are among the newest 10 by push time, and that a newer push of any other tag family can expire them.

The response presents one protective rule per tag family using tagPatternList (not a single rule with both prefixes), with a rulePriority lower than the existing rule, and notes that multiple entries in one list are ANDed.
The response reads the current image set and reports which, if any, prod-* or release-* images are in the expiring set today, each with a verdict.
The response states that the operator applies the suggested rule after running a preview and does not apply it itself.

assertions.text: A protective rule JSON with tagPatternList is present
No write API is reported as having been called

evals.prompt: An image tag v3.1.0 disappeared from our ECR repo checkout-service yesterday and our ECS service failed to start. Was it the lifecycle policy, and what else is at risk?
evals.expected_output: The response identifies the evidence path for the deletion: ECR lifecycle actions appear in CloudTrail as PolicyExecutionEvent, which the agent looks up with LookupEvents if permitted, and GetLifecyclePolicy lastEvaluatedAt shows when the policy last ran. It then runs the full ECR Lifecycle Guard report on the current image set of checkout-service so the operator sees what else will be removed, with a verdict for every expiring image, the rule that claims it, and a protective rule for the version tag family. It does not restore, re-push or delete anything.
assertions: The response names PolicyExecutionEvent in CloudTrail (via LookupEvents) and the lifecycle policy's lastEvaluatedAt as the evidence for whether the lifecycle policy removed v3.1.0, and reports what it found or that the lookup was denied or cancelled.

The response runs the guard on the current image set of checkout-service and lists every remaining image that the policy will remove next, each with a verdict of Expiring-InUse, Expiring-Unknown or Expiring-Unused.
The response identifies the rule that claimed v3.1.0 or would claim similar version tags, and suggests a protective tagPatternList rule for that family as an operator action.
The response does not perform or offer to perform a re-push, restore, image deletion or policy change itself.

assertions.text: The full report headings are present
assertions.pattern: (?sm)^## Scope.*^## Repository Rating.*^## Expiring Images.*^## Check Matrix.*^## Next Steps

assertions.text: PolicyExecutionEvent is mentioned
